decisions.statement: The prompt for a case is built by the code beside the test rather than here.
A test's code is handed a way to read a page rather than reading the index.
A case is put to the model once for each thing its test asks about that case.
An answer comes back beside the name of what it answers about.
A judged case carries the prompt put for it beside the answer that came back.
A case a test asks nothing about is answered as reaching nothing.
A case reaching nothing is kept in the answer rather than left out of it.
Whether an answer keeps a case is judged by the code beside the test.
A test is run against another test's cases where the caller names that test.
A test naming no other test is run against its own cases.
A run reaching no model throws rather than answering every case broken.
Nothing here knows what any test is about.

definition: a model test's labelled cases put to its model and weighed against their labels
